title: The Sky Opens
mood: The sky over the bay tears open, Enders pour into the city, and one post on the channel never answers.

hero.alt: Purple four-pointed portals open across a dark storm sky over the city's towers; then a tall gray Ender, landed from the sky, rises close in front of the towers.

segs.t: Lesley stood at the window with her rifle on her shoulder. The command deck sat over the command room, high in the Academy’s tower, under the glass lab. Its long window faced the bay.
Out past the dome’s seaward edge, the small magenta star was coming apart.
Its four points pulled away from each other. The sky between them tore into a ragged mouth, rimmed in magenta. The clouds over the bay leaned toward it, and the gray morning went dark as dusk.
“Sound it,” said Lesley.
The alarm went up through the tower. A breath later, sirens answered in every ward.

Over the waterfront, purple portals opened out of thin air. Enders leapt through them, tall and gray, and dropped onto the warehouse roofs. Behind Lesley’s visor, her machine eye laid thin teal lines over them as they landed.
They were inside the dome.
The dome was the Defensive Bubble, the energy shell over all of Terrinia. Until today, an army had to claw its way in from outside.
Chang’e sat at her console behind her, Mr. Bunny at her shoulder. Small crescents turned in the air around her chair. She was already reading.
“The dome’s open over the waterfront,” she said. “The Singularity tore it.”
On the Academy’s tallest tower, the Energy System’s rings spun faster. Its white-cyan beam fed the dome, and it climbed and climbed. The hole over the water did not close.
“It can’t hold against a door that size,” said Chang’e.

She opened a file from the oldest records the Academy kept. It was a shaking film of a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky. Under the film ran the storm readings taken with it. She laid today’s readings over them.
The two lines sat one on top of the other.
“They match,” said Chang’e. “This is the Storm Citadel’s storm.”
Lesley looked out. Rain and black cloud hung over the water. Violet light moved inside it.
“There’s no ship.”
“No.”
“Then where is it coming from?”
Chang’e touched the ragged mouth on her screen. “Through the Singularity. From the other side.”
“The records say that storm kills every machine under it.” Lesley keyed the command channel. “All posts. Report.”
“Gate, clear.”
“Infirmary, clear.”
Every voice came back clean.

The last time she saw that violet, she was standing on a windowsill. Downstairs, a radio had stopped in the middle of a word. Only the clocks her father wound by hand had kept ticking. Her thumb found the bolt under the coil, the old action, and stayed there.
“It’s only the edge of it,” said Chang’e.
Lesley did not know why the channel held. She used it.
Behind the first wave, a second line had begun to climb on Chang’e’s screen.
It was slow and far away, and it was larger than anything on the console. Chang’e frowned. She opened VOID NOTES, her file on the void, still marked
working on it
, and laid it over the line.
Nothing else she had matched it. Her notes on the void matched it at three points.
“Something larger is coming through after them.” She swallowed. “It’s a guess, Big Sis. Only a guess.”
“Logged,” said Lesley. “Keep reading.”
One more trace ran along the bottom of the screen, thin and faint. It matched nothing at all, not even the notes. Chang’e watched it. Then she logged it with no name.
“Posts,” said Lesley.
Chang’e had them ready.
“Fanny, Layla, Guinevere: frontline assault. They meet the Enders head on.”
“Ruby and Angela: rear support.”
Rear support held the ground just behind the frontline: Angela’s shield, the wounded, the way out.
“Selena: mobile support.” Chang’e tapped Silverbolt’s icon on the screen, twice. “Her machine is the fastest in my division.”
Mobile support went wherever the fight bent.
Lesley stood behind Chang’e’s chair now, one hand resting on its back. Chang’e let it stay.
“Send it,” said Lesley.
The names went out over the open channel.

blocks.caption: The posts, as the Academy’s battle report logs them.

media.alt: A battle report card: the Singularity opens and the alarm sounds; small portraits mark Lesley and Chang'e at command, Selena on mobile support, Fanny, Layla and Guinevere on the frontline, and Ruby and Angela in rear support.

segs.t: On the map, the red marks came in at the waterfront, where the dome was torn. Then every one of them turned inland, for the Academy’s wards. Nothing anywhere else.

Years ago she had stood on a roof over a burning city. Every swarm leaned on the edge of her district, and every defender ran to meet them. Far off, one giant walked through the middle of the city where nobody stood. The blow fell on the base by the water. She came too late.
They don’t want the city,
she thought.
They want us out in the streets, meeting them. Then the real blow lands here, where nobody stands.
She wanted a roof and a line of sight. She stayed at the console.
“Shield reserves, hold your wards,” she said on the channel. “Nobody moves without my word.”
The reserves answered, one by one.
“Mobile support,” said Lesley. “Report.”
Nothing answered.
“Her frame’s fast,” said Chang’e. “She’ll answer when she gets there.”
Lesley looked at the light one breath longer. “Log it.”
On the panel, the light for mobile support kept blinking.
The bell tower.
The wind wanted Selena off the tiles. She let it try.
She had come up between classes, while everyone else crowded the hologram wall. Her boots hung over a drop full of sirens. Silverbolt had hooked its claws over the gutter beside her.

blocks.caption: Selena on the bell tower, Silverbolt beside her.

media.alt: Selena in her school uniform sits on the edge of a high ledge under a storm sky, her boots over the drop, her dragon-shaped machine Silverbolt crouched beside her.

segs.t: On the stairs up she had started a new lollipop.
In her ear, the channel had said her name.
Selena: mobile support.
Then Lesley’s voice:
Mobile support. Report.
Under the Academy’s call ran the other one, the recall. For weeks it had burned in her cells, pulling her toward the sky over the bay. Today it pulled from the open mouth itself.
In her pocket, the recall buzzed on her phone too. Red, no sender. She did not take it out.
She answered neither.
Below her, Enders kept dropping out of the purple portals over the waterfront. They came down onto the roofs and into the streets, and spread from there toward the Academy. The sirens wound higher.
Selena smiled at all of it.
“I’m the type who shines in chaos,” she told Silverbolt.
Silverbolt said nothing. It had no voice.
Somebody wins today,
she thought.
Them or us. Whoever us is.
She had already turned both roads down: back to the Mother Matrix and the huntress behind that pull, or dying for humanity.
Mobile support. Right in the middle of the board.
No, thanks. My road’s my own. I’ll sit this one out till I see how the pieces fall.
Down in the courtyard, the frontline was forming. Shield soldiers and students in suits stood in ranks. A long cannon caught the lightning.
Among them stood a girl with a long pink ponytail, two cat-eared drones at her shoulders.
The girl put her hand to her collar.
